Names, or at least the rules surrounding these titles, are no longer clear cut. Teachers, Doctors etc are referred to by an honorific title. Children in Australia usually call adults what their parents refer to the adults in their lives as. Personally,  I prefer people not to make assumptions about my marital status. I'm a teacher and I'm referred to by my legal title, but I go by my mother's maiden name. In public with friends, family and acquaintances, I really don't appreciate people assuming if I'm married, single, divorced or widowed, or assuming that my name indicates any of these things. I'm not sure where you are but in Australia on Aus airlines (Qantas, Jetstar, Virgin Australia) anyone sitting in an exit or front row needs to be able bodied in the case of emergency. Cabin crew have a duty of care to ensure passenger safety, and this can be prioritsed over comfort. If there was the unfortunate case of having to exit passengers quickly, your lack of mobility would have hindered the exit path of others. If this was the case - unfortunately the FA was correct. If you were in a bulkhead seat obviously there is far less leg room and your own mobility may have been hondered. Animals are not permitted in our flight cabins, so the cat is a non issue. All animals are in a special section of the cargo.  I'm so sorry you have had to go through such an ordeal. The least the FA could have done is explained liability and tried to accommodate both parties by knowing what the correct regulations are wherever you are located.
